findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required argument — won't compile
findings.body: The new condition `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` with no arguments, but the only definition in the hierarchy (in `UsernamePasswordForm`) is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No zero-arg overload exists in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, `UsernamePasswordForm`, `WebAuthnAuthenticator`, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`, or `AuthenticatorUtils`. This will fail to compile. The intended call is almost certainly `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which would also match the surrounding logic (only skip the re-auth form when passkeys are NOT enabled, so the form is shown for passkey re-auth). As written the PR cannot build and the whole change is blocked.

findings.title: Broker fallback path bypassed when conditional passkeys are enabled
findings.body: With the new guard `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, the `hasLinkedBrokers` short-circuit is only evaluated when passkeys are disabled. When a user has no passkey credential but DOES have a linked identity provider, and conditional passkeys are enabled at the realm level, the code falls through to `super.authenticate(context)` and the user is presented with a username-only form from which they cannot complete re-authentication (no passkey available, broker not consulted). The original `if (!this.hasLinkedBrokers(context))` skip-success path needs to remain available in that scenario, e.g. by checking broker availability independently of passkey enablement.

findings.title: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate now requires webauthnAuth to be non-null in the re-auth path
findings.body: The new unconditional call `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }` is placed outside the `else` branch and uses the new helper that only returns true when `webauthnAuth != null`, so the NPE guard is preserved. However, the no-arg `UsernamePasswordForm()` constructor (still present in the file) leaves `webauthnAuth = null`; if any flow instantiates the authenticator via the deprecated no-arg constructor and then enters the re-auth branch (where `context.getUser() != null`), the helper short-circuits and the code works, but the dead `webauthnAuth` reference in the old `if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())` block in the same method has been removed. The old guard protected against the no-arg-constructor case; the new code relies entirely on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returning false when `webauthnAuth` is null, which is correct, but this invariant should be asserted or the no-arg constructor removed to avoid future regressions.

findings.title: WebAuthn form re-rendered on every password error even when no passkey is registered
findings.body: `challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String)` now calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, i.e. whenever a user is in context and passkeys are realm-enabled. This is invoked from `badPasswordHandler` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` for every wrong-password attempt. For users who have no WebAuthn/passwordless credential registered, the page will still render the conditional-UI WebAuthn affordance and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm` will set `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI=true` and issue a fresh challenge. This is confusing UX and potentially reveals feature availability. The new `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` only covers the case where passkeys are disabled at realm level; there is no test for the case where passkeys are realm-enabled but the specific user has no passkey credential, and the new code will incorrectly show the WebAuthn option in that scenario.

findings.title: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH visibility widened from protected to public
findings.body: The constant `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is changed from `protected static final` to `public static final` solely so that `AuthenticatorUtils` in a different package can read it via a static import. This expands the public API surface of the abstract authenticator for an internal coordination flag. The cleaner alternative is to keep the constant package-private (or protected) and expose a small accessor (e.g. `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` is already protected and could be made public/util-style), or have `AuthenticatorUtils` accept the boolean as a parameter rather than reaching into the constant. As-is, any external code can now read and write the auth note under that key, which is an internal protocol between authenticators.

findings.title: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError silently no-ops when auth note is absent
findings.body: The new `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` reads the auth note and only sets the form attributes if `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)` is true. If the note was never set, or was set to a non-boolean value (e.g. a string from a buggy caller — note that the producers in `UsernamePasswordForm` use the literal string `"true"`, which is fine, but the constant is now public so any caller can write anything), the method silently does nothing without logging. Given this is being called from error paths in both `badPasswordHandler` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`, a missing or malformed value should at minimum be logged at debug level so a maintainer can diagnose why a re-auth form is rendering with the username field visible.

findings.title: Assertion against driver.findElement is unreachable on the success path
findings.body: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the test does `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue());` followed by `fail(...)`. `Selenium WebDriver.findElement` never returns null — it throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is absent, so the `assertThat` line is never reached in the expected case; the `fail` is also unreachable because the catch block already swallows `Exception`. The test passes only because the `catch (Exception nsee)` block catches the `NoSuchElementException`. Use `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` (which is the pattern used elsewhere in the same file before this PR) for clarity, and remove the dead `assertThat` + `fail`.

findings.title: No test for re-authentication when user has passkeys disabled at user level
findings.body: The new `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` covers the case where passkeys are disabled at the realm level, and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` covers a user with both passkey and password. There is no test for the intermediate case: a realm with passkeys enabled and a user who has the passkeyless policy applied but has not actually registered a WebAuthn credential. Given the new code paths in `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` and `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge` will render the WebAuthn conditional UI for such a user on re-auth (because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true and the WebAuthn flow does not check whether the user actually has a WebAuthn credential at that point), this scenario should be explicitly covered to prevent a regression where the form is shown but no authenticator can satisfy it.
